description: Evidence table for classifying non-receptor polymer chains. Chain length and proximity to the receptor are NOT classification criteria — a nanobody and a peptide ligand can be the same length, and a transducer sits closer to the receptor than most ligands do. Identity evidence (UniProt accession, entity description) decides; length is recorded but never decides.
precedence: 1. receptor identity: UniProt accession matches the structure's GPCRdb receptor accession
2. curated UniProt accession match (transducer / fusion / arrestin)
forbidden_rules: classify a protein as ligand because it contacts the receptor
assume the shortest non-receptor chain is the ligand
assume any chain that is not receptor or transducer is a ligand

receptor_identification.primary_rule: A polymer entity is a receptor instance when its UniProt accession set contains the accession of the structure's GPCRdb-assigned receptor.
receptor_identification.chimera_rule: Receptor entities frequently also carry a fusion accession (e.g. 'Adenosine receptor A2a,Soluble cytochrome b562,Adenosine receptor A2a' carries both P29274 and P0ABE7). Such an entity remains ONE receptor instance; the fusion is recorded as construct engineering, not as a separate ligand or partner chain.
receptor_identification.fallback_rule: Where accession evidence is absent, the GPCRdb preferred_chain is used to identify the receptor chain, and mapping_confidence is set to 'chain_annotation_only'.
receptor_identification.failure_rule: If neither applies, receptor_mapping_status = unresolved and the record is queued for review.

description_patterns.rationale: Covers all G-protein subunits and engineered mini-G / chimeric constructs across species. Extended in Phase 2 after audit: entities are also described as 'G subunit alpha (q)' and 'G subunit q (Gi1-Gq chimeric)', which the original phrase did not match.

Matched case-insensitively because the same reagent appears with many spellings in this dataset: scFv16 occurs as scFv16, scFV16, ScFv16, scfv16, 'Antibody fragment scFv16' and 'single Fab chain (svFv16)'; Nb35 occurs as Nanobody 35, Nanobody35, Nanobody-35, nanobody Nb35 and Nb35. Extended in Phase 2 after audit of unclassified chains: the dataset also contains 'Camelid antibody VHH fragment', 'NabFab HC/LC', 'FabH', 'FabL', 'Single-chain Fv16', 'Single-Chain Fragment Variable 16' and the depositor typo 'Nanoboy 35'.
Standard crystallisation fusion partners, whether separate chains or chimeric segments. Extended in Phase 2: 'Thioredoxin 1' appears as a solubilisation fusion in this dataset.

Identified partners that are neither ligand, transducer, antibody nor fusion. Extended in Phase 2: GRK1/GRK2 ('Rhodopsin kinase GRK1', 'Beta-adrenergic receptor kinase 1') and the FKBP1A/calcineurin pair used in molecular-glue structures are identified partners, neither ligand nor transducer.

polymer_ligand_rule.rule: A polymer chain is a pharmacological ligand ONLY when the structure's source ligand annotation (GPCRdb) carries type 'peptide' or 'protein' and the chain is not already identified as receptor, transducer, antibody or fusion.
polymer_ligand_rule.matching: Where exactly one unclassified non-receptor polymer chain remains and the source annotates a peptide/protein ligand, that chain is the ligand with confidence 'single_candidate_match'. Where more than one remains, every candidate is emitted with confidence 'ambiguous_multiple_candidates' and queued for review — the pipeline does not pick one.
polymer_ligand_rule.segment_rule: Whether the whole chain or only a segment is the interacting ligand is a separate field, recorded as unresolved unless a source states the range. It is never inferred from geometry.

peptide_length_threshold.not_used_for: deciding whether a chain is a ligand
peptide_length_threshold.rationale: A conventional cut-off for reporting only. Chain length has no role in role assignment: Nb35 is 128 residues and endothelin-1 is 21, but so are many engineered fragments.

description_regex_rules.rationale: Short depositor codes for nanobodies and megabodies, e.g. 'Nb6', 'CNb36', 'NBA3', 'MB52'. Anchored to the whole description so it cannot match a substring of a real protein name.

rule_change_log.change: Extended description patterns for transducer, antibody, fusion and auxiliary roles, and added anchored regex rules for short nanobody codes.
rule_change_log.trigger: Audit of the 382 polymer chains left unresolved by the first pass showed four systematic identity gaps rather than genuinely unknown chains.
rule_change_log.principle: Every addition is identity evidence — a reagent's name or accession. No pattern uses chain length or proximity to the receptor.
